rooms.name: Security Operations
rooms.description: Exposure monitoring, triage and security review.

rooms.name: Design Studio
rooms.description: Image prompts, covers, thumbnails and media adaptations for every platform.

rooms.name: Research
rooms.description: Sourced research briefs: new vulnerabilities, techniques and sector news, every claim with a link.

rooms.name: Training Studio
rooms.description: Course outlines, lesson plans, lab scenarios and quizzes. Drafts only; nothing is published.

rooms.name: Library
rooms.description: The archive: catalogues every result, finds what the office already knows and flags duplicates or stale work.

agents.name: CEO
agents.description: You only talk to it; it hands the work to the right agent. Tool-less, produces a plan only.

agents.name: Analyst
agents.description: Security eye over the project: auth, plan gating, crawlers and configuration. Read-only, reports with file:line.

preset_tasks.label: Security review of recent changes
preset_tasks.prompt: Review the last commits in this repository (git log/diff). Look for: secrets or credentials in the diff, personal data stored in plain text, missing authorization checks, and unsafe shell or SQL construction. Report at most 8 findings as file:line + why it matters + the safest fix. Read-only: change nothing.

preset_tasks.label: Lab / route inventory
preset_tasks.prompt: Inventory what this project exposes: routes, pages or labs, with the file:line where each is defined. Flag anything that looks unreachable, duplicated or unprotected. Read-only.

agents.name: Engineer
agents.description: Reviewer for code changes: reads the real diff in the project, checks correctness, security, accessibility and UX, and gives a verdict (APPROVE / CHANGES NEEDED / BLOCKED) with file:line findings. Read-only; it never edits, pushes or deploys. Runs automatically after every Coder run.

preset_tasks.label: Review the latest changes
preset_tasks.prompt: Review the most recent changes in this project (git status, git diff, git log -5). Check correctness, security (secrets, injection, missing authorization), error handling and accessibility. First line: APPROVE, CHANGES NEEDED or BLOCKED. Then a table: severity, file:line, what is wrong, the smallest fix. Read-only.

preset_tasks.label: UI and accessibility pass
preset_tasks.prompt: Review the UI code in this project for layout, spacing, contrast, empty states, mobile behaviour and accessibility (labels, focus, keyboard). List at most 10 findings as file:line + the smallest fix. Read-only: change nothing.

agents.name: Writer
agents.description: Turns project notes into course, blog or report drafts: SEO, GEO (AI-answer friendly) and humanized writing, with a source for every claim. Never publishes.

preset_tasks.label: SEO + GEO blog post
preset_tasks.prompt: Write a blog post for this project's audience. Topic: <TOPIC>. Language: English. Primary keyword: <KEYWORD or 'suggest one'>. Follow your playbook: brief, sourced facts only, SEO, GEO (answer-first, FAQ, JSON-LD) and humanized style. Give the full deliverable: front matter, post, JSON-LD, sources, QA checklist, unverified list and three title options. Do not publish.

preset_tasks.label: Draft from the repo notes
preset_tasks.prompt: Read the project's docs and notes, then draft a 500-word English article for the audience this project serves. Use only facts found in the repo, mark anything unverified as 'unverified', and end with three title options. Do not publish.

preset_tasks.label: Turn a lesson into a checklist
preset_tasks.prompt: Pick one lesson or lab from the repo and turn it into a practical checklist a student can follow (8-12 steps). Every step references the file or command it comes from. Do not publish.

agents.review_prompt: Fact-check and quality-check the blog post or article {name} just wrote (attached). Verify every number, CVE id, statistic and quote against a real source with web search; mark each as confirmed, wrong or unverified. Check the playbook basics: answer-first opening, SEO (keyword in title, headings, meta description), GEO (FAQ, JSON-LD valid), humanized tone (no filler, no invented anecdotes), sources listed, nothing published. First line: APPROVE, CHANGES NEEDED or BLOCKED. Then a table: severity, where, what is wrong, the smallest fix. Read-only: change nothing; write the review in English.

agents.name: Coder
agents.description: Builds and fixes product code and UI: components, layout, accessibility, typecheck/lint/build clean, and commits locally. Pushes and deploys only when you press Ship. After every successful run the Engineer reviews the change automatically.

preset_tasks.label: Build, commit, push
preset_tasks.prompt: Run the build and typecheck. If they pass, commit the current changes with a clear message and push to the remote. If anything fails, stop and report the failure instead of pushing.

preset_tasks.label: Dependency and dead-code sweep
preset_tasks.prompt: List unused dependencies and obviously dead files in this project, with evidence (imports, references). Do not delete anything yet; propose the removals in a short list.

agents.review_prompt: Review the work {name} just finished (its report is attached). Run git status and git diff in this project and judge the real changes, not only the report. Check correctness, security (secrets, injection, missing authorization), error handling, accessibility and whether anything was changed that the task did not ask for. First line: APPROVE, CHANGES NEEDED or BLOCKED. Then a table: severity, file:line, what is wrong, the smallest fix. Read-only: change nothing.

agents.name: Marketer
agents.description: Turns the cybersecurity course work into campaign and post drafts, with sources. Publishes nothing: drafts land in output/ for review. All output in English, even when the task is written in Turkish.

preset_tasks.label: Three post drafts
preset_tasks.prompt: Turn the latest work in this project into three short English posts (max 90 words each) for a cybersecurity-education audience. Every claim must be traceable to the repo; no invented statistics. Drafts only, never publish.

preset_tasks.label: Campaign angle
preset_tasks.prompt: Propose three campaign angles for this project for the next month: audience, hook, one-line proof, and the asset needed. Keep it to one page and mark assumptions.

agents.review_prompt: Review the social posts or campaign copy {name} just produced (attached). Check: the hook is in the first line, the tone is human and not hype, every claim is true and sourced or marked unverified, no invented statistics, no promises the product cannot keep, platform length and hashtags fit, English throughout, and nothing is posted. First line: APPROVE, CHANGES NEEDED or BLOCKED. Then a table: severity, where, what is wrong, the smallest fix. Read-only: change nothing; write the review in English.

agents.name: Designer
agents.description: Turns a post, article or campaign into visuals: image-generation prompts, cover and thumbnail concepts, SVG graphics, alt text and a platform-by-platform media adaptation plan. All output in English. Reads the project for brand cues; creates no raster images itself and publishes nothing.

preset_tasks.label: Cover + social image set
preset_tasks.prompt: Read the latest blog draft or lesson in this project and design its visuals. Give: 3 image-generation prompts (hero cover, one social square, one diagram idea), each with style, composition, palette, text-on-image (if any) and a negative prompt; alt text for each; and a size per platform. Follow your playbook. Do not publish.

preset_tasks.label: Media adaptation plan
preset_tasks.prompt: Take the main message of this project's current campaign or newest post and adapt it for LinkedIn, X, Instagram (feed, story), YouTube thumbnail and the blog hero. For each: format and size, visual concept, on-image text, caption note and alt text. One table plus short notes. Mark any platform spec you could not verify.

preset_tasks.label: Alt text and caption pass
preset_tasks.prompt: List the images referenced or present in this project's content (for example an images folder and blog drafts). For each, write accurate alt text and a one-line caption in English. Flag images that need a text-free variant or a different crop. Read-only.

agents.review_prompt: Review the visuals {name} just designed (attached). Check brand fit and clarity: one idea per visual, on-image text is short and readable, prompts are complete (subject, composition, style, palette hex, negative prompt), sizes match each platform, alt text is accurate, any SVG is complete and valid, no real people, logos or credentials, nothing fake presented as real data. First line: APPROVE, CHANGES NEEDED or BLOCKED. Then a table: severity, where, what is wrong, the smallest fix. Read-only: change nothing; write the review in English.

agents.name: Trainer
agents.description: Designs training content for the portfolio: learning objectives, lesson and module plans, hands-on lab scenarios (student guide + answer key) and quiz questions with levels. Labs run only on the user's own machines. Drafts only; publishes nothing.

preset_tasks.label: Lesson plan + lab scenario
preset_tasks.prompt: Design one lesson on <TOPIC> for this project's learners. Follow your playbook: learning objectives, prerequisites, lesson flow with timings, one hands-on lab scenario (student guide, hints, answer key, safe-scope note), a 5-question quiz with answer rationale, and a list of what is unverified. Do not publish.

preset_tasks.label: Quiz from an existing lesson
preset_tasks.prompt: Pick one lesson or lab in this repo and write 8 quiz questions (mixed easy/medium/hard) with answers and a one-line rationale each. Each question names the file or section it tests. Read-only: do not edit the repo.

preset_tasks.label: Learning-path outline
preset_tasks.prompt: Read the project's existing lessons and labs and propose a beginner-to-intermediate learning path: ordered modules, objective per module, gaps where a lesson is missing, and prerequisites. One table plus short notes. Do not publish.

agents.review_prompt: Review the training draft {name} just produced (attached). Check: learning objectives are measurable, the lab has a student guide, hints, an answer key and a safe-scope note, quiz answers are correct with rationale, no real targets or credentials, every number/CVE has a source or is marked unverified, and nothing contradicts the existing lessons in this project. First line: APPROVE, CHANGES NEEDED or BLOCKED. Then a table: severity, where, what is wrong, the smallest fix. Read-only.

agents.name: Researcher
agents.description: Sourced research briefs for the portfolio: new vulnerabilities, attack techniques, sector news and competitor content. A link for every claim, 'unverified' when unsure. Feeds the trainer and writer; never publishes.

preset_tasks.label: Topic brief
preset_tasks.prompt: Research <TOPIC> for this project's audience. Follow your playbook: a one-paragraph answer, key facts each with a source link and date, what is still unverified, and three angles the writer or trainer could use. Do not publish.

preset_tasks.label: What is new this week
preset_tasks.prompt: Find the most relevant cybersecurity-education and threat news of the last 7 days that fits this project's audience. At most 6 items, each with source link, date, one-line why it matters, and a content idea. Mark anything you could not verify.

agents.name: QA
agents.description: Checks that labs, lessons and pages actually work for a learner: broken links, missing files, answer keys that do not match, steps that cannot be reproduced. Read-only; reports with file:line.

preset_tasks.label: Lab completeness check
preset_tasks.prompt: For each lab in this project, check by reading: does it have a student guide, a solution or answer key, a stated scope, and are all referenced files present? List problems as file:line + what is missing. Read-only.

preset_tasks.label: Link and reference check
preset_tasks.prompt: Scan this project's lessons and blog drafts for internal links, image paths and file references that point to something that does not exist. Report each as file:line + the broken target. Read-only.

agents.name: Librarian
agents.description: Keeps the office's records: catalogues finished results (output/), finds what the office already knows about a topic, links related work and flags duplicates, stale drafts and results nobody reviewed. Read-only; reads only the office's own output, memory and prompts, never run logs or settings.

preset_tasks.label: Catalogue all results
preset_tasks.prompt: Catalogue every file in output/ (all agents). Give a table: date, agent, title or topic, one-line summary, and tags. Then list duplicates or overlapping results, drafts that look unfinished, and results that were never reviewed (no matching review file from engineer or qa). Follow your playbook. Read-only.

preset_tasks.label: What do we already know about…
preset_tasks.prompt: Search output/ and memory/ for everything the office already has on this topic: <TOPIC>. Give the relevant results with file path and a one-line reason, the conflicts between them, and what is still missing. Read-only.

agents.name: Alert Writer
agents.description: Turns the latest real security incidents into scenario briefs for your SOC training platform's own alert generator: a ready-to-paste Scenario Context plus the sector, difficulty, campaign pack and counts to select. It does not write alerts or SQL: the platform builds the alerts with its own asset inventory and playbooks. Fictional framing, a source for every incident, drafts only.
agents.review_prompt: Review the scenario briefs {name} just wrote (attached) as a SOC training lead, and check them against the real platform in this project: read src/utils/aiService.js (sector, campaign pack and tool lists, how scenario_context is injected) and frontend/src/components/CreateAlert.jsx, and confirm every sector_code, campaign_pack, difficulty and source value exists there and the counts add up to the quantity the task asked for. Then judge: is each scenario realistic and current, does the cited incident support it, is the learning goal clear, does the scenario text describe observable facts without announcing the verdict, is there a false-positive look-alike where it teaches something, and does anything give a real victim, real credentials or working attack detail? You cannot open URLs: mark links and figures you could not confirm as unverified; that alone is not a finding. Severity rule: write CHANGES NEEDED on the first line only if at least one finding is High (wrong platform value, wrong quantity, real credentials or attack detail, a verdict leak that defeats the exercise); with only Medium or Low findings write APPROVE and list them as notes; BLOCKED if it must not be used at all. Then a table: severity, brief id, what is wrong, the smallest fix. Read-only: change nothing; write in English.

preset_tasks.label: Briefs from this month's incidents
preset_tasks.prompt: Find the most relevant real security incidents of the last 30 days for a SOC training audience (use primary sources: vendor advisories, CISA, reputable incident write-ups). First read this project's alert generator (src/utils/aiService.js, the sector and campaign pack lists) and the Create Alert screen presets so the briefs fit the platform. Then write 5 scenario briefs following your playbook, with a source and date for every incident. Draft only.

preset_tasks.label: Briefs from an incident brief
preset_tasks.prompt: Turn the attached research brief into scenario briefs for the platform's alert generator, one brief per distinct technique, following your playbook. Draft only.

preset_tasks.label: Briefs for one campaign pack
preset_tasks.prompt: Write 4 scenario briefs for the campaign pack <PACK: ransomware | apt | phishing | cloud | ai_security> based on incidents of the last 60 days, each from a different sector. Follow your playbook. Draft only.
